title: Trend line splits the range by day, week, month or quarter correctly
custom_preconds:
1. Sign in on the build under test as an Admin user. Admin holds every permission, including Reports, so Reports and Dashboard both show in the top menu.
  2. In the top bar choose a location with more than two years of invoices, so Revenue has a value in every period.
  3. Click Dashboard in the top menu. You will set custom ranges on the Revenue tile: click its range pill, click a start day and an end day in the calendar, check the "Range: N days" readout at the bottom, then click Apply.
custom_steps:
1. On Revenue set a custom range of exactly 31 days (readout "Range: 31 days"). Hover along the trend line (or count the points) and write down how many points there are and the date each shows.
  2. Set a range of exactly 32 days and do the same.
  3. Set ranges of exactly 182 days and then 183 days and do the same.
  4. Set ranges of exactly 731 days and then 732 days and do the same.
  5. On the 31-day range hover one point and write down its date and value. Open Reports > Sales, set the Date to that single day, and write down the Totals row Subtotal.
  6. On the Technician Utilization tile set a custom range that includes a day on which nobody clocked time (check Reports > Timesheet Activities, e.g. a Sunday) between days that do have clocked time. Look at the trend line around that day.
  7. On the Technician Utilization tile set a custom range in which only one day has clocked time (e.g. a single working day). Look at where the trend line would be.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • 31 days: one point per day (31 points). 32 days: one point per week.
  • 182 days: one point per week. 183 days: one point per month.
  • 731 days: one point per month. 732 days: one point per quarter.
  • The hovered day's value equals the Sales report total for that single day.
  • The day with no clocked time leaves a gap in the line: the line is not joined across it and does not drop to zero.
  • With only one day that has a value, no line is drawn. In its place the tile shows the empty-chart placeholder: a light grey dashed outline with rounded corners, no fill and a grey line-chart icon in the middle, the same height as a trend line. The headline still shows its figure.
  • If the trend line shows no dates or values on hover, count the points (zoom the browser in if needed) and write "values not checked by hand" in the result comment for the value check.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-490; story SV-9576 (S4); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850 v42, read 7 Oct 2026, S4 (S4-R11, S4-R12). Design canvas (claude.ai/artifact/Wae9DFQ8PJQBy8mbLsL5ge, captured 2026-09-28) used for on-screen labels and navigation only: boards 03_Range_After (calendar, presets, "Range: N days" readout, Apply). Design canvas row 15 (15_Empty_Design, approved 2026-10-07, to build) shows the empty-chart placeholder.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S4-R11: “The sparkline draws one point per bucket, and the bucket size is chosen from the length of the selected range: a range of 31 days or fewer buckets by day; 32 to 182 days by week; 183 to 731 days by month; anything longer by quarter. Each point is the measure recomputed over that bucket using the same calculation as the headline, so a point can never disagree with the tile it sits in. A bucket for which the measure has no value (S3-E3) contributes no point, and interior gaps are preserved rather than closed up or drawn as zero. When fewer than two points have values, no line is drawn and the tile shows the empty-chart placeholder instead (S4-R12).”
  • S4-R12: “A tile shows the empty-chart placeholder in place of its sparkline when fewer than two points in the selected range have a value.”
